learning_outcomes.text: He/she can realize the relationship between material science and engineering.
he/she can understand the mechanical properties of materials and determine the materials' defects.
He/she can estimate the behaviour of materials at different conditions and can select the proper material for different applications by knowing the materials structure.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Types of material. The importance of material selection.
Atomic structure and atomic bonding. Crystal structures. Lattice structures. Directions, planes, Miller indices. Linear and planar atomic density.
Deformation. Deformation mechanisms. Effects on mechanical behavior of crystal structure defects.
The tensile test. Tensile specimens, test equipment, test results, toughness, resilience. Cold deformation.

Cold deformation (continued). Strain hardening. Strain hardening rate. Grain size effect. Strain aging hardening. Baushinger effect. Significant yield. High temperature deformation. Climbing, creep mechanisms. Fracture. The coefficient of anisotropy (r). The importance of the application.
Compression, bending, torsion tests and practical importances. Hardness tests. Mohs, Brinell, Rocwell hardness tests.
Impact testing. Charpy, Izod impact tests. Test temperature. Factors affecting the fracture energy. Applications.
Properties of metals. Alloys. Phase diagrams. Phase diagrams of alloys.
Binary phase diagrams. Solubility. Technical applications.
Phase diagrams of alloys (continued). Eutectic phase diagrams.
bibliography: Donald R Askeland, "The Science and Engineering of Materials"
Ahmet Aran, Materials Science Lecture Notes.
William F. Smith, Materials Science and Engineering.
